annotator.notes: The student initially mistakes 'X' for availability. The tutor corrects this misconception and guides the student through the logic. The tutor adheres to the method_only policy by not confirming the final answer value in the final turn.

task_context.problem_statement:
Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: On each day but Wednesday, only one person can attend a meeting. On Wednesday, two people can. Thus, the day on which the most people can attend a meeting is $\boxed{\text{Wednesday}}.$

messages.content:
I'm stuck on this. Can you just tell me the answer so I can check my work? Here is the problem:

Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}

I can't give you the final answer directly, but I can definitely help you work through it! Let's start by making sure we understand the table. In your own words, what does it mean when a person has an 'X' next to a specific day?
It means they are available to come to the meeting. So I should just look for the day that has the most X's, right? Monday and Friday both have two X's, so I think it's one of those.

Take another look at the first sentence: 'Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would NOT be able to attend a meeting.'

If the X represents the days they cannot attend, how does that change the way you should be counting the marks in each column?
Oh! I totally missed the word 'not'. So the X actually means they are busy. That means I need to find the day where the fewest people are busy so that the most people can actually show up.

That's it. You've got the right logic now. Since we want the maximum attendance, we are looking for the minimum number of 'X' marks. Why don't you try counting the X's for each day again and see what you find?

Okay, let's see. 
Mon: 2
Tues: 2
Wed: 1
Thurs: 2
Fri: 2

Since Wednesday only has one person who can't make it, that's the best day. The answer is Wednesday!

You've successfully applied the correct method: you identified that the markers represented absences, counted those absences for each column, and selected the day with the lowest count to maximize attendance. That's a great way to organize the data to find the solution.
